The plasma-sprayed TBC system consists of a low-pressure plasma-sprayed (LPPS) NiCrAlY or CoCrAlY bond coating and an air-plasma-sprayed yttria (8%) partially stabilized zirconia insulative layer.
The EB-PVD TBC system has a NiCoCrAlY bond coating and a yttria (20%) stabilized zirconia insulative layer.
Plasma-sprayed TBCs achieve strain tolerance through 10-15% porosity and subcritical microcracking in the zirconia layer.
EB-PVD TBCs achieve strain tolerance through a columnar microstructure in the zirconia layer.
Fracture toughness values for plasma-sprayed yttria-stabilized zirconia coatings range from 0.5 to 3.2 MPa√m.
Laser glazing of the EB-PVD zirconia surface can significantly improve durability in the presence of molten salt films.
Burner rig tests have shown EB-PVD yttria-stabilized zirconia coatings can withstand over 29,000 thermal cycles without failure.
The program includes development of thermomechanical and thermochemical life prediction models for both plasma-sprayed and EB-PVD TBC systems.
High-pressure turbine blades have been coated with the program TBC systems for a factory engine test to validate the life models.
Eddy current technology has been shown to be feasible for nondestructively measuring zirconia layer thickness in TBC systems.
